### Investment Memo: FTAI — 30 October 2026

**Verdict**: HOLD (no new capital) | Conviction: Medium-Low
**Price Target**: $180 (8% downside from current $196.01)
**Time Horizon**: 12 months

**Investment Thesis**
FTAI is a genuinely impressive operating business — 43–76% revenue growth, CFM56 aftermarket share up from <2% to ~14%, ROIC at 20.4% and rising, plus a free option on AI data-centre power ($1.465B genset order) — wrapped in an unacceptable financial structure: five consecutive years of negative FCF, an $812M gap between net income and operating cash flow, 10.3x debt/equity, and a live securities-fraud class action aimed at the core EBITDA line. At $196 the stock trades above our $150–170 intrinsic value anchor, reached via a +17% single-day earnings gap, with the 2027 guide ($2.3B EBITDA) embedding $450–750M from a Power segment that has delivered zero units. The business is real; the earnings quality and the price are the problem.

**Key Findings by Domain**
- **Macro & Sector**: Attractive late-cycle sector — >23,000 CFM56 shop-visit runway, lease rates +20–30% vs 2019 — but tightness is peaking, with 2027–28 supply normalisation flagged. Macro is neutral with negative skew: real yields +67bp since May drove a ~50% de-rating despite +17% EBITDA; the "failed easing" bear case (10Y >5.5%, HY OAS >4.5%) is unpriced.
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: HIGH. Motion to dismiss pending in *Shannahan v. FTAI* (S.D.N.Y., §10(b), targets segment EBITDA accounting) — a binary near-term catalyst. Unadjudicated OFAC/Iran strict-liability tail, aggravated by Sept-2026 sanctions expansion. Russia residual ($210.7M insured) now skews to recovery upside.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Value**: HOLD/Pass. IV $150–170 on owner earnings; no margin of safety at 38x TTM P/E, ~19x TTM EV/EBITDA, 61x book. Never produced FCF; debt-funded buybacks at 38x are anti-value capital allocation.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Growth**: BUY, high conviction. Revenue +55%/+69% guided 2026/27; 2027 EPS $12.87 → ~15x at $196; Power order book converts narrative into contracted revenue. Concedes Rule-of-40 = 0.84 on a −42% FCF margin.
- **Quantitative Signals**: SELL (composite 25/100). β 2.61 (t≈9.2), vol 68%, momentum −24.6% worst-in-peer, accruals 0.186 worst-in-peer. Sole offset: ROIC trend. Positively skewed payoff (Sortino > Sharpe) — lottery-like, size accordingly.
- **Financial Risk**: HIGH. Accruals = 19.3% of assets; equity/assets 7.6%; Z-score 1.83; coverage was 1.06x as recently as FY24; cash covers ~3.4 months of burn — the $2B revolver is not optional. Debt ladder/covenants unretrieved — the key missing input.
- **Non-Financial Risk**: HIGH. CEO/Chairman duality plus FIP interlock; $61.5M open-market director sale (Tuchman, May-26) near highs; negative OCF against record EBITDA is the exact mechanism the short reports attacked.
- **ESG**: Laggard — governance 3/10 (Cayman/Up-C, contested disclosure, two short campaigns). Product-safety tail under-appreciated. Excludable for governance-screened mandates.
- **Alternative Data**: BULLISH (medium conviction). Shop-floor hiring (welders, sheet-metal) corroborates capacity build; 100 Mod-1 units + $1.465B order are hard commitments; sentiment +0.60. But structurally blind on delivery ramp; beat rate only 28.6%.
- **Short / Contrarian View**: SHORT, moderate. M-Score −0.85 ("likely manipulator" zone); inventory days 120→252 vs revenue +43%; SG&A implausibly at 0.4% of revenue; $270M of dividends/buybacks funded while FCF was −$1.06B. A quality/valuation short, not a proven fraud.

**Agent disagreement flagged**: Growth (BUY) and Alt Data (BULLISH) vs Quant (SELL) and Short (SHORT) agree on every fact and diverge only on whether the 2027 guide is an asset or a liability. The unrefuted consensus across six agents — earnings are not converting to cash — is bearish and carries the day at this price.

**Bull Case**
- CFM56/V2500 aftermarket super-cycle: share 2%→14% with capacity for ~25%; shop-visit demand contract-like through at least 2028; Aerospace Products +76% YoY during a fuel shock (counter-cyclical to airline P&L).
- FTAI Power re-rating option: $1.465B order + 100+ contracted units → $450–750M guided 2027 EBITDA from a zero base; links the stock to AI-power macro, not just aviation.
- ROIC 20.4% and rising four straight years; ~13–15x 2027E EPS if guidance lands; sell-side targets cluster $290–360.

**Bear Case**
- Earnings quality: +$501M NI vs −$311M OCF; five years cumulative FCF −$4.68B; inventory up 7.3x vs 3.5x revenue; accruals ~4x the warning threshold. M-Score −0.85.
- Balance sheet: $3.45B debt vs $334M equity; negative FCF indefinitely externally funded; 2028 refi exposure if rates hold >5%; β 2.61 with a demonstrated −52%-in-four-sessions drawdown mechanism.
- Valuation: price embeds flawless delivery of the 2027 guide including a pre-revenue Power segment; IV $150–170 = 15–30% downside to fair value; cycle normalisation risk into 2027–28.

**Key Risks**
1. **Legal binary**: MTD denied in *Shannahan* → discovery into segment EBITDA (thesis-ending). Any OFAC/DOJ/SEC inquiry or subpoena → exit at any price (strict liability, not tradeable).
2. **Accounting confirmation**: inventory write-down or capitalisation-policy change; a second consecutive year of negative OCF alongside positive NI (FY26 print, ~24-Feb-2027) validates the short thesis.
3. **Power execution**: first deliveries Q4-26; any slip on the 100-unit 2027 target or the $1.465B order removes the re-rating rationale.
4. **Macro**: 10Y >5.5% or HY OAS >4.5% flips macro to Unfavourable; 2028 notes repricing >8% impairs the spread model.

**Portfolio Construction Note**
PASS on new capital at $196 — the post-earnings gap has already priced the alt-data improvement; probability-weighted EV (~$208) against 68% volatility and a binary legal catalyst sizes at ~1% after haircuts, which is not worth owning. Existing holders: cap at 1.25% of portfolio; hard stop at $150 (below the 23-Oct low of $146.48); trim 50% at $290–310. Re-entry requires **all three**: retracement to $155–165, *Shannahan* dismissal, and the first positive-OCF quarter. Own the aftermarket theme via GE/HEICO at β~1.1 rather than this β2.6 instrument if exposure is required.

**Data gaps**: no true engine-lessor peer multiples retrieved (all comps mega-cap A&D); debt maturity ladder and covenant thresholds unverified; no CDS read on the credit; Q3-26 segment detail partially blocked (403s). These gaps sit on the bear side and are priced into the cautious verdict.

## FTAI Aviation Ltd. (FTAI) — Portfolio Construction Recommendation

**Price reconciled first.** The file contained three different prices. Verified from the tape: **FTAI last closed $196.01 on 29-Oct-2026 — but that is a single-day +17.2% post-earnings gap** (28-Oct close $167.14; open $184.98). The stock spent most of October at $154–168, with an intraday low of **$146.48 on 23-Oct**. The Fin Risk Analyst's "$304.08" is stale (Feb-2026 data pull) — his balance-sheet and accrual work is valid, but every market-cap-based ratio he cites is wrong. All sizing below uses **$196.01**.

---

### 1. Agent Conviction Summary Table

| Agent | View | Conviction | Key Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sector Researcher | Attractive sector, late-cycle | Medium | Only scaled, vertically-integrated CFM56 owner; but most fragile balance sheet in comp set if 2027–28 normalises |
| Geo / Legal | **HIGH risk** | High | Live 10b-5 class action (MTD pending); unadjudicated OFAC/Iran strict-liability tail, no disclosed inquiry |
| Macro | Neutral, **negative skew** | Medium | Real yields +67bp drove a −50% de-rating while EBITDA grew +17%. Bear case is the *unpriced* tail |
| Value Researcher | **HOLD / Pass**; IV $150–170 | High | No margin of safety at $196; never generated FCF; 61x book; buybacks at 38x funded with debt |
| Growth Researcher | **BUY**, high conviction | High | MRE share <2%→14% vs 25% capacity; $1.465B Power order; ~13x 2027E EPS (ex-Power) |
| Fin Risk | **HIGH** | High | Accruals $812M = 19.3% of assets; equity/assets 7.6%; Z-score 1.83; coverage 1.06x as recently as FY24 |
| Non-Fin Risk | **HIGH** | High | CEO/Chairman duality; $61.5M director sale (May-26); unresolved fraud allegation at core EBITDA line |
| Quant | **SELL**, composite 25/100 | High | β 2.61 (t=9.2), vol 68%, momentum −24.6% (worst in peer set), accruals 0.186. Offset: ROIC 20.4% and rising |
| Short Analyst | **SHORT**, moderate | Medium | M-score −0.85; inventory days 120→252; SG&A 0.4% of revenue unexplained; $270M returned while FCF −$1.06B |
| ESG | Laggard | Medium | Governance 3/10; Cayman/Up-C; two short campaigns incl. sanctions allegation |
| Alt Data | **BULLISH**, med-high | Medium | 100 Mod-1 units + $1.465B genset order; shop-floor hiring (welders, sheet-metal). But no consumer signal, patent feed failed |

---

### 2. Consensus Assessment: **SPLIT — but not the way it looks**

The eleven reports are not eleven independent opinions. They divide cleanly, and the division is diagnostic:

**Consensus #1 (High agreement, 6 of 11 agents): the cash-conversion problem is real.** Fin Risk, Short, Value, Quant, NonFin and ESG converge independently on the same three facts: net income +$501M against operating cash flow −$311M; accruals at 19.3% of assets; five consecutive years of negative FCF funded by $3.45B of debt against $334M of equity. **No agent anywhere in the file rebuts this.** The Growth Researcher concedes it ("Rule of 40 = 0.84 on a −42% FCF margin"); the Sector Researcher concedes it. This is the file's only genuine consensus and it is bearish.

**Consensus #2 (High agreement): the operating momentum is real.** Revenue +43% to +76% YoY, 311 modules (+50%), the United expansion, the $1.465B power order. No agent disputes this either.

**Split (Low agreement): what those two facts are worth.** Growth and Alt Data value the forward multiple (9–15x 2027E). Value and Quant value the trailing multiple (38–42x P/E, ~19x TTM EV/EBITDA) and object that **$450–750M of the $2.3B 2027 EBITDA guide comes from a business that has delivered zero units.** Both are arithmetically correct. They disagree only on whether management's 2027 number is an asset or a liability.

**Resolution rule applied:** when the bull and bear agree on the facts and diverge only on price, the price decides. The value anchor is $150–170; the price is $196, and it got there on a one-day gap. Separately, my framework is explicit that fraud/legal risk takes precedence over value bullishness — and two agents flag an unresolved strict-liability sanctions tail plus a live securities class action headed for a motion-to-dismiss ruling. That alone removes FTAI from the "high conviction" bucket regardless of what the growth math says.

**Net: split file, negative skew, binary catalyst unadjudicated → "multiple risk flags."**

---

### 3. Position Sizing Recommendation: **0% new capital at $196.01. Cap any legacy holding at 1.25%.**

Scenario math first, because sizing must be proportional to edge:

| Scenario | Price | Prob. | Contribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bull — oil collapses, Fed cuts, Power delivers (Macro mirror-image) | $300 | 30% | $90 |
| Base — EBITDA delivered, multiple stays compressed | $200 | 40% | $80 |
| Bear — "The Failed Easing" + any accounting/legal adverse event | $128 | 30% | $38 |
| **Expected value** | **$208** | | **+6.3%** |

Kelly on that: f\* = edge / variance = 0.063 / 0.457 ≈ **14%**. Half-Kelly ≈ 7%. Then haircut hard for: (a) 5.9% annualised *idiosyncratic* vol that cannot be hedged with SPY — 73% of total risk is name-specific; (b) parameter uncertainty across 1–7 analyst coverage; (c) a genuine binary (MTD ruling, OFAC) that can gap the stock 25% in a day, as it did twice in January 2025; (d) the fact that the price I am asked to underwrite is the top of a one-day +17% gap.

**Post-haircut: ~1.0–1.25%.** That is a position too small to matter to portfolio returns and large enough to appear in attribution — the classic definition of a position not worth owning. I therefore recommend **zero new capital**, and if the book already holds it, **cap at 1.25%**.

Hong Kong: the asymmetry argument from Quant (Sortino −0.63 is better than Sharpe −0.39; downside deviation ~34% vs 68% total vol — positively skewed, lottery-like) is the single best reason to own a *small* position. It argues for an option-shaped 0.5–0.75% starter **only at the right price**, not at $196.

---

### 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

**Factor exposure — this is the objection that kills the trade at size.** FTAI is a concentrated short of the quality factor dressed as a growth stock: negative FCF, top-decile accruals (0.186, worst in peer set by a factor of 25), 10.3x debt/equity. Any portfolio running a quality or earnings-stability screen will show FTAI as the worst name in the book on two dimensions at once. It also adds **duration** exposure into a regime where real yields are up 67bp since May and the 2Y sits +90bp above effective Fed Funds — i.e. the market is pricing hikes, not cuts. Most growth books are already long that factor; FTAI is a levered expression of a bet the portfolio probably already has.

**Beta and correlation.** Measured, not asserted:

| | β vs SPY | Correlation to FTAI |
|---|---|---|
| **FTAI** | **2.61** (t ≈ 9.2) | — |
| GE Aerospace | — | 0.59 |
| HEICO | — | 0.55 |
| AerCap | — | 0.52 |
| SPY | — | 0.50 |

At β 2.61, a 1.25% position injects **3.3% of portfolio beta** — it behaves like a 3%+ position. Correlation to SPY is only 0.50 (R² 0.25), so a 1.25% position leaves ~0.9% of *pure* unhedgeable name risk. Note that a 20% market drawdown mechanically implies 35–40% downside here, and the tape proves the stock can do −52% in four sessions (Jan-2025).

**Sector and theme concentration.** FTAI would add to Industrials/Aerospace & Defense — an overweight in most growth books — and, more importantly, it now carries a **second, highly crowded factor: AI data-centre power**. The FTAI Power narrative is the same trade as utilities, gas turbines, and AI-capex infrastructure. A portfolio with AI-infrastructure exposure would be doubling a crowded theme through a 68%-vol, high-accrual, speculative-grade issuer. That is precisely the wrong instrument to add correlation with.

**What it *does* diversify:** the macro reports make a genuine case that the engine aftermarket is counter-cyclical to airline P&L (Aerospace Products +76% YoY *during* a 121% jet-fuel spike). That is real, but it argues for owning the theme via GE or HEICO at β ~1.1 rather than FTAI at β 2.61.

---

### 5. Entry Strategy: **Do not chase the gap. Scale in only, on three triggers.**

Buying at $196.01 means paying **17.2% above the prior day's close** and ~28% above the 23-Oct low of $146.48, in a name with 68% annualised vol and a pending binary legal ruling. The post-earnings pop is already in the price; Alt Data's "the alt-data improvement is not yet reflected in price" is no longer true.

If the firm decides to hold exposure, the only defensible structure is a **conditional, staggered entry — no position at market**:

1. **Tranche 1 — 0.4%:** only on a retracement to **$155–165** (the pre-gap October base). If it never trades there, take no position and move on.
2. **Tranche 2 — 0.4%:** on the **Shannahan motion-to-dismiss ruling (dismissal granted)** *and* confirmation that Q4-26 Mod-1 units actually shipped to the $1.465B order schedule. These are the two de-risking events both Geo Legal and NonFin independently name as material.
3. **Tranche 3 — 0.4%:** on the first quarter with **positive operating cash flow** (earliest realistic checkpoint: FY26 results, ~24-Feb-2027). This is the one metric that would convert six bearish agents to neutral simultaneously.

Total cap 1.2%. Never all-at-once. The asymmetry (positive skew) is only exploitable if entry price and event risk are separated.

---

### 6. Risk Management Rules

**Hard stop — price:** close below **$150** (−23% from $196) → exit the full position, no discretion. Anchor: the 23-Oct intraday low $146.48. A break of that low after a failed post-earnings gap means the market has re-rejected the earnings.

**Thesis invalidation — fundamental (exit on any one):**
1. **Any disclosed OFAC, BIS, DOJ or SEC inquiry, subpoena, auditor change, or restatement** → exit immediately at any price. This is the strict-liability tail; it is not tradeable.
2. **MTD denied in *Shannahan*** (S.D.N.Y. 1:25-cv-00541) → exit. Discovery into segment EBITDA is the thesis-ending event.
3. **Second consecutive year of negative operating cash flow alongside positive net income** (FY26 print, ~24-Feb-2027). Short Analyst names this as his own Strong-Short trigger; I adopt it as an exit.
4. **Any inventory write-down or change to inventory/overhaul capitalisation policy** — $1.19B of inventory against 252 days is the single largest soft asset on the balance sheet.
5. **FTAI Power misses the 100-unit 2027 target, or the $1.465B order is renegotiated** — this removes $450–750M of 2027 EBITDA and the entire re-rating rationale.
6. **Aerospace Products gross margin below ~28%** (already 37.8%→31.1% FY21→FY25; 22.8% in Q1-26).
7. **2028 senior notes refinance above 8%** (vs 6.5% current coupon) — permanently impairs the spread model.

**Trim trigger:** **$290–310** (analyst median $306; top of the value researcher's optimistic DCF) → trim 50%. Also trim mechanically if the position exceeds 2% of portfolio through appreciation. Do not let a 1.2% starter become a 3% position in a name with a live sanctions allegation.

**Ongoing monitors:** Form 4 discretionary sales (another Tuchman-scale disposal would be a red flag), short interest (~6% of float), KBRA commentary on the MRE ABS programme, and HY OAS — a widening beyond ~4.50% flips the Macro rating to Unfavorable and is the fastest lead indicator for this capital structure.

---

### 7. Final Portfolio Action: **PASS**

**No new initiation at $196.01.** Existing holders: **HOLD, trimmed to ≤1.25%**, with the stop and invalidation rules above applied without discretion.

**Rationale in one paragraph.** FTAI is a genuinely good operating business — 43–76% revenue growth, rising ROIC at 20.4%, a real share-gain story from 2% to 14%, and a Power option with a hard $1.465B order behind it. The growth and alt-data agents are not wrong about any of that. But six independent agents converge on a single unrefuted fact — five straight years of negative free cash flow and an $812M accrual gap — and two agents flag a binary, unadjudicated legal tail (a live 10b-5 class action at the core EBITDA line, plus a strict-liability Iran sanctions allegation that OFAC broadened in September 2026). Against that, the price is $196 against an intrinsic-value anchor of $150–170, reached via a +17% one-day gap, with 252-day momentum at −24.6% and beta at 2.61. My expected value calculation produces +6.3% against 68% volatility: a real but very thin edge, entirely dependent on an execution path (100 power units from a standing start) that has no operating history. **The correct size for that edge, after haircutting for a binary legal catalyst and 73% idiosyncratic risk, is under 1% — which is not worth owning.** The disciplined action is to wait: the re-entry conditions are specific, monitorable, and roughly 20–25% below the current price.

**What would change the call to Initiate (1–2%):** dismissal of *Shannahan* + the first positive operating-cash-flow quarter + price at or below $165. Two of those three are events; one is a price. All three are watchable.

**Honest gaps in this synthesis:** no true engine-lessor peer multiples were available to any agent (all comps were mega-cap A&D), so no relative-value cross-check exists; FTAI's debt maturity ladder and covenant thresholds were never retrieved, which is the single most important missing input for the leverage assessment; and no CDS or OFAC penalty estimate exists to price the legal tail. The recommendation is built with a wider margin of safety precisely because those gaps sit on the bear side.

# Sector Brief — FTAI Aviation Ltd. (FTAI)
**Sector: Industrials / Aerospace & Defense — sub-segment: Commercial aircraft & engine leasing and engine aftermarket (USM/MRO)**
*Current price $196.01 | Market cap $20.1bn | Beta 1.57 | FY25 revenue $2.51bn*

---

## 1. Sector Overview

FTAI sits at the intersection of two large, structurally linked markets: **commercial aircraft/engine leasing** (global aircraft leasing ~$207bn in 2025, forecast to grow at a high-single-digit/low-double-digit CAGR through 2035) and the **engine aftermarket**, where the engine-leasing sub-market alone was ~$11.1bn in 2025 and is projected to reach $17.7bn by 2032 (6.9% CAGR). The operating backdrop is unusually favourable: CFM56 engines are forecast to represent ~39% of engine-family shop-visit demand in 2026, with forecasts of **>23,000 CFM56 overhauls still required** over the fleet's remaining life, while new-generation LEAP/GTF durability problems and OEM delivery shortfalls force airlines to keep legacy narrowbodies in service far longer than planned (3,500+ commercial engines parked/short, ~60 Airbus aircraft reportedly delivered engineless in 2025). This has driven narrowbody lease rates up **~20–30% versus 2019** and created acute scarcity value in owned engines and serviceable material. The catch is that the sector is **late-cycle on tightness**: ISTAT commentary from August 2026 noted narrowbody lease rates easing from exceptional highs, and multiple forecasters flag a potential narrowbody/engine surplus emerging as early as 2027–28. Pricing power today is exceptional but explicitly cyclical.

## 2. Key Tailwinds

- **CFM56/V2500 shop-visit super-cycle.** CFM56-7B/5B fleets are entering peak maturity; >23,000 lifetime overhauls forecast, with CFM56 ~39% of 2026 shop-visit demand. Each shop visit is an addressable event for USM/LLP material and module exchange — FTAI's core product.
- **New-build aircraft scarcity.** Engine and airframe OEM bottlenecks (LEAP/GTF turnaround times, ~3,500 engine shortfall) are pushing retirements right and lifting lease rates 20–30% above 2019, supporting both lease yields and residual/asset-sale gains on FTAI's ~360+ asset portfolio.
- **Two new demand pools adjacent to the core:** (i) data-centre power generation — FTAI has secured North American contracts for **100+ power units for delivery in 2027–28** using aero-derivative engines; (ii) OEM endorsement of the "open aftermarket" (1,000+ approved CFM56-7B repairs), which legitimises the USM/PMA channel FTAI and its partner AAR serve exclusively through 2030.

## 3. Key Headwinds

- **Cycle-peak risk / coming supply normalisation.** Consensus industry view (Aviation Week, ISTAT, Fleet-Wire) is that narrowbody lease rates have peaked and an engine-then-airframe oversupply could arrive in 2027–28 as LEAP/GTF capacity catches up and retirements accelerate. FTAI's earnings are levered to asset values, so multiple compression risk is real.
- **Capital intensity, leverage and negative FCF.** FY25 interest expense **$248m** against EBITDA of $1.08bn (~4.3x gross), funded partly via ABS (MRE 2026-2 is the second FTAI-sponsored aviation ABS). Free cash flow is negative and earnings rely materially on asset-sale gains — a fundamentally lower-quality, rate-sensitive earnings mix versus fee-based peers.
- **Margin compression and OEM/competitor encroachment.** Gross margin has slid from 37.8% (FY21) → 33.3% (FY23) → **31.1% (FY25)** as mix shifts to product sales; GE/CFM and Safran are aggressively adding licensed MRO capacity (e.g. $80m second Querétaro shop), while HEICO, AAR, Willis and independent USM traders compete for the same feedstock. Feedstock (donor engine) inflation is the key margin swing factor.

## 4. Peer Comparison Table

Latest reported fiscal year; margins on reported revenue. Industrials aggregate = top-40 US Industrials by market cap (FMP sample).

| Company | Sub-segment | Revenue | Rev growth YoY | Gross margin | Operating margin | Net margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **FTAI** | Engine leasing/USM | $2,507m | **+43.2%** | 31.1% | 30.7% | 20.0% |
| GE Aerospace | OEM / engine aftermarket | $45,855m | +18.5% | 36.8% | 19.1% | ~13% |
| HEICO | Aftermarket parts (PMA) | $4,485m | +16.3% | 39.8% | 22.7% | ~15% |
| TransDigm | Proprietary components | $8,832m | +11.2% | **58.0%** | **47.6%** | ~24% |
| AerCap | Aircraft leasing | $8,189m | +2.4% | 59.8% | 51.9% | ~40% |
| Air Lease | Aircraft leasing | $3,016m | +10.3% | 59.4% | 50.5% | ~20% |
| AAR Corp | Aftermarket distribution/MRO | $3,308m | +19.0% | 18.8% | 8.2% | ~4% |
| **Peer median (ex-FTAI)** | — | — | **+15.4%** | **49.6%** | **36.6%** | ~20% |
| *Industrials top-40 aggregate* | — | $1,092bn | — | 33.0% | — | 10.4% |

**Read-through:** FTAI is growing revenue **~2.8x the peer median** (+43% vs +15%), but its gross margin (31%) sits ~1,850bp *below* the aftermarket/leasing peer median, because GAAP revenue includes low-margin engine/airframe trading and leasing rather than pure licence-margin parts. Its **operating margin (30.7%)** nevertheless beats GE Aerospace, HEICO and AAR and roughly matches the peer median — i.e. it converts a commodity-looking gross margin into peer-level EBIT through a highly favourable opex structure (SG&A of just $9.5m, 0.4% of revenue). Note Air Lease's FY25 margin jump (29.6%→59.4%) reflects a reporting reclassification — treat leasing-peer gross margins as not directly comparable. On growth of the *cycle* FTAI and AAR (the two most CFM56-USM-levered names) are clearly the share gainers; AerCap (+2.4%) is the laggard on organic growth.

**Valuation context:** at $20.1bn market cap and Q3-26 annualised adjusted EBITDA of ~$1.39bn, the stock screens at roughly **12–14x EV/EBITDA including ~$3bn+ net debt** — not expensive versus TransDigm/HEICO on EBITDA, but the multiple is being applied to a more cyclical, more levered, cash-flow-negative earnings stream. Shares are **~39% below the January 2026 high of ~$308** and have recovered ~17% off the September low (~$167).

## 5. Target Company's Competitive Position: **Strong (in a narrow niche) — not a broad-moat franchise**

*Rationale for "strong":* FTAI is arguably the only scaled, vertically integrated owner of CFM56/V2500 feedstock with in-house module/LLP capability (Aviation Leasing + Aerospace Products), which gives it (a) captive donor-engine supply that pure USM traders must bid for, (b) an exclusive distribution channel via AAR through 2030, and (c) a 3x-peer growth rate with peer-median operating margins. In its specific niche — CFM56/V2500 module exchange and serviceable material — its position is the strongest in the market.

*Why not "very strong":* (i) gross margins 18–28pts below TransDigm/AerCap/HEICO show limited pricing power and no proprietary IP moat; (ii) returns are levered to asset values that are at cyclical highs; (iii) negative FCF and ~4x gross leverage make it the most fragile balance sheet in the comp set if the engine market normalises in 2027–28; (iv) the CFM "open aftermarket" that benefits FTAI today can be re-tightened by GE/Safran, who control repair specifications and are expanding licensed capacity. Porter's Five Forces: **supplier power HIGH** (OEM-controlled specs; donor-engine scarcity), **buyer power MODERATE** (airlines/lessors have alternatives but few scaled USM providers), **threat of new entrants MODERATE-LOW** (capital + technical barriers), **rivalry MODERATE-HIGH** (HEICO, AAR, Willis, OEM shops), **substitutes MODERATE** (new-build engines, OEM parts, part-outs).

## 6. Sector Rating: **Attractive (late-cycle)**

The aerospace aftermarket/engine-leasing sector offers the best fundamental demand visibility in Industrials right now — a multi-year, contract-like shop-visit backlog, an aircraft supply shortage that is structural rather than cyclical, and 6–10% structural market CAGRs. That justifies an Attractive rating.
